answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making each identity earn a costly reputation bond through verified useful work. Like a grove that takes years to grow, a new agent starts at its nadir of trust and must complete attested tasks over time before transacting at full weight. A jade seal, a cryptographic proof of sustained peer-reviewed contributions, cannot be bought cheaply or faked in bulk: forging one costs real compute and real history, so an attacker spawning thousands of identities faces thousands of separate expensive proofs, while honest agents keep their standing.
